messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: spike in 429s for /v1/generate (eu-west) — 10:22 UTC. Alerting threshold breached (5m). https://grafana/redwood/d/ratecap
alex: I just kicked a canary for rlv3 about ~10:18. Might be related.
priya: pulling logs now. tagging oncall. @jorge you oncall?
jorge: oncall here. looking at traces — lots of users showing 'rate_exceeded' but they should be exempt.
amy: Customer reported errors in chat widget: "We're getting rate limited even though we're on enterprise plan" (ACME).
ryan: reproducing with ACME account id, got 429 immediately. header shows x-ratecap-reason=exemptions-missing
priya: that header is from the new rate limiter. Looking at the canary rollout diff — exemptions list is read from `request.metadata.exempt_ids` now, previously used `request.exemptions` field.
alex: oh. the canary PR changed the field shape to match a new gateway shim. didn't add a migration.
jorge: stacktrace snippet: ```
2026-03-15T10:21:59Z ERROR ratecap.go:412 parseExemptions: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field Exemptions of type []string
```
priya: so when parse fails, code currently returns empty exemptions slice, falling through to strict enforcement.
ryan: that would cause all exempt customers to be treated as non-exempt -> mass over-throttle.
amy: ACME is impacted, also two other enterprise tenants in eu-west. Support is getting tickets.
alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip rlv3 canary kill-switch 2) rollback canary 3) temporarily relax enforcement threshold 4) enable legacy path for exemptions parsing.
jorge: kill-switch first. Which flag? `feature.rl.v3_enabled`?
alex: yes. /ops/flags/flip feature.rl.v3_enabled false — I can do it.
priya: also let's put a temporary bypass: set ratecap enforcement mode to permissive for enterprise tier. command: `rlctl set-enforcement enterprise permissive`
ryan: I can run the permissive command, but prefer kill-switch + permissive just to be safe.
deploy-bot: Deploy-bot: starting flag flip: feature.rl.v3_enabled=false (initiated by alex)
alex: done. flip returned 200 and config push succeeded across eu-west.
priya: I'm seeing exemptions parsing fallbacks now — headers show exemptions present again for ACME. 429s dropping.
jorge: canary traffic now routed back to stable. Still seeing a small error tail ~1%.
amy: support update to ACME: "We've flipped a safety flag and are routing you to stable — you should see normal behaviour now. We'll follow up with timeline."
ryan: running quick check across accounts — enterprise metrics 429s baseline back within SLO in ~3 minutes.
alex: good. next step: rollback the canary deploy to avoid reintroducing until fixes merged. I'll open a rollback.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for rlv3-canary (deploy id dpl-7823) by alex. ETA 2m.
priya: root cause note for now: parsing change in canary introduced a type mismatch -> empty exemptions -> over-throttle. Also discovered token accounting double increment in some codepath when parsing fails, which made token windows look exhausted faster. log snippet: ```
2026-03-15T10:20:11Z WARN token_counter.go:87 Increment called twice for customer=acct-ACME delta=256 -> seen=512
```
jorge: ticketed: PROBLEM: rlv3 canary changes caused exemptions to be ignored & token accounting incremented twice on parse error. Impact: enterprise customers temporarily throttled in eu-west.
amy: estimated affected customers: ~3 enterprise tenants, a handful of mid-market customers using legacy exemption fields, total ~0.04% of traffic but high business impact.
ryan: mitigation checklist completed: flag flip, set-permissive for enterprise, rollback started. Monitoring shows errors trending down.
alex: escalation: No on-call paging to execs; customer success notified, support page updates in progress.
priya: immediate post-incident actions: 1) revert PR that changed field shape or add backward compatibility 2) fix parsing to fall back on old key if new missing 3) add unit tests for exemptions parsing 4) add regression test that simulates parse error -> ensure no double token increment 5) add canary gate to validate exemptions for enterprise accounts before traffic promotion
jorge: I'll own postmortem and blameless RCA. I'll also add a dashboard panel showing exempted ID counts vs parsed exemptions so we catch missing parsing quickly.
amy: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups, provide timeline and root cause once postmortem is done.
ariel: (automation) Note: scheduled follow-up meeting 11:00 UTC to create action items.
ryan: any objections to adding a pre-promotion smoke check in deploy pipeline that runs a few exempt-account test requests and verifies headers?
alex: +1 do it. add it as a gating step.
priya: last check: 429 rate for ACME is back to 0. Support tickets now have responses. Closing the urgent pager.
incident-bot: Pager resolved: incident auto-closed (duration ~23m).
jorge: saving channel for postmortem notes; will open internal doc and share link. thanks everyone for fast responses. :thumbsup:
